theorem.statement: For every finite admissible design class, the certified Pareto frontier is exactly computable by finite enumeration, certified infeasibility pruning, and certified dominance pruning.  A candidate may be discarded without running its remaining certificate tasks whenever a proved upper envelope for all of its attainable objective coordinates is weakly dominated, with one strict coordinate, by the proved lower objective vector of an already certified candidate.  After all unpruned candidates terminate, pairwise comparison of their certified output vectors returns exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  No assumption in the frozen core guarantees a strict reduction from exhaustive evaluation in the worst case: all admissible candidates can remain feasible and mutually nondominated.
theorem.proof_tex:
The caps make \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\) finite.  Indeed there are finitely many choices of \(J\), finitely many matrices in \(\{0,\ldots,m_{\max}\}^{J\times K}\), finitely many nonempty grid subsets of the finite set \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) with size at most \(L_{\max}\), finitely many declared allocations and well caps, and finitely many integer truncation, moment, Taylor, subdivision, and precision choices under \(\mathfrak b\).  The constraint \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\leq B_{\max}\) only removes candidates.  Write the resulting set as \(\{\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_N\}\).

For a certified candidate define the maximization-oriented vector
\[
 y(\Xi)=\bigl(\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\kappa_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\mu_{\mathcal T},
 -N_{\mathrm{req}},-w_{\mathrm{cert}},-\mathfrak B(\Xi)\bigr). \tag{33}
\]
Order candidates by their finite encodings.  First apply the exact syntax, rank, simplex, box, and arithmetic-cap tests.  Maintain the set \(C\) of completed certified candidates.  If interval calculations for an unfinished candidate \(x\) prove an upper envelope \(U(x)\) satisfying \(y(x)\preceq U(x)\) for every possible certified completion, and some \(c\in C\) satisfies \(y(c)\succeq U(x)\) with one strict coordinate, discard \(x\).  This is sound because transitivity gives \(y(c)\succeq y(x)\) with a strict coordinate.  Otherwise run the remaining finite certificate tasks.  When all unpruned candidates have terminated, delete from \(C\) each candidate dominated by another member of \(C\).

The one-sided conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness\text{-}complexity}\) validate every infeasibility decision and every bound used in this comparison.  A pruned candidate cannot be Pareto maximal.  Every retained candidate is certified and is not dominated by any certified candidate, because the final comparison is exhaustive over all certified, unpruned completions.  Conversely, a certified nondominated candidate can be neither soundly infeasible nor soundly dominated by an envelope, so it survives.  The returned set is exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).

Nothing in the frozen assumptions forces a candidate to be infeasible or dominated before its certificate tasks are evaluated.  For an explicit generic-class certificate, take an admissible instance whose finite candidate sets and caps leave a singleton \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}=\{\Xi\}\) and for which \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\).  Its frontier is \(\{\Xi\}\), and its only candidate must undergo the tests establishing certification.  More generally, if all certified vectors (33) are pairwise incomparable, dominance pruning removes none.  Therefore the algorithm is exact and its pruning rules can be useful, but no strict worst-case reduction from exhaustive evaluation follows without an additional structural dominance theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. Any recovered count-valued law in the published pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification. The capped certified-design frontier is exactly computable by finite enumeration with sound infeasibility and dominance pruning, but the assumptions guarantee no strict worst-case saving over exhaustive evaluation. The three-node base and conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery, proves causal minimality of the strict positive-polynomial benchmark directly from its positive edge coefficients, and supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating one-sided-sound certifier. Over every capped finite admissible class, finite enumeration, sound infeasibility pruning, sound dominance pruning, and final comparison compute the exact certified Pareto frontier, although no strict worst-case pruning gain is guaranteed. Relative eventual certification is proved only under explicit strict exact slack and uniform convergence of all numerical controls; no prescribed synthetic input is claimed to meet those premises.

prose_updates.interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law; it does not define a graph or an intervention. The recovered law identifies a labeled DAG on the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class. Intervention contrasts require the narrower causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, whose full support identifies the kernels in the truncated factorization. The certificate handle enumerates the declared finite design class, records all three statuses, and promotes only \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) inputs to Pareto comparison. A candidate is pruned only when a proved attainable upper envelope is dominated, with one strict coordinate, by an already certified lower objective vector; final comparison of all surviving certified candidates returns exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\). Fixed controls always terminate but can remain undecided, and every admissible input may require evaluation in the worst case. Along a control sequence, eventual certification follows only from the separately stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The leaf ceiling and outward-rounded operation bound are unconditional finite ceilings, not efficiency guarantees. The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot and its two pointwise Jacobian singular values certify neither compact-box graph separation nor remote identification, chart coverage, tails, covariance, or useful contrast precision. In the remote-pair eventual-certification argument, on the compact parameter-pair set \(K\) define the exact moment distance \(f\), the constraint \(D=\lVert\theta-\theta'\rVert_2^2-r_{\mathrm{id}}^2\), the remote set \(S=\{D\geq0\}\), and \(U=\{f>\lambda_*/2\}\). Strict remote slack gives \(S\subset U\); hence the compact complement \(K\setminus U\) is disjoint from \(S\), and continuity yields one \(\delta>0\) such that \(D\leq-\delta\) there. Uniform continuity and a sufficiently fine finite mesh then put every leaf in one of two valid cases: a leaf disjoint from \(K\setminus U\) lies in \(U\) and passes by a positive lower enclosure for \(f\), while a leaf meeting \(K\setminus U\) has a negative upper enclosure for \(D\) and is discarded. Thus no uniform negative margin is inferred merely from containment in the varying open set \(\{D<0\}\). Without the stipulated strict margins and convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and rounding controls, the procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). Neither fixed synthetic input currently has a validated proof object, and finite-frontier pruning has no guaranteed strict worst-case advantage.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies to recovered laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM class and imposes no Poisson source law. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid construction, certification, and Wald inference are confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\). Certification is always terminating and one-sided sound but may be undecided. The exact capped Pareto frontier is obtained by finite enumeration with sound pruning; the result does not promise that pruning avoids exhaustive evaluation. Eventual certification is conditional on strict positive exact graph, remote, chart, Jacobian, interiority, algebraic, and precision margins together with uniform numerical convergence; it certifies neither prescribed benchmark by itself. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared-well dependence, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem converts the finite capped design class into an exact auditable Pareto computation with explicitly sound pruning rules.
statement_notes.gap: Certified upper-envelope pruning can reduce work instance by instance, but the frozen assumptions impose neither universal infeasibility nor universal dominance, so they imply no strict worst-case reduction from exhaustive evaluation.
statement_notes.consumer: It yields a reusable finite menu of nondominated certified prospective designs and records when every candidate still has to be evaluated.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the substantive entries of \(\Xi\) and the sequence \((\Xi_t)\) from the statement.  All graph-specific parameter boxes and their pairwise products are compact, and there are only finitely many graph tuples.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), the exact moment maps and all derivatives used by the procedure are continuous on these boxes.  The stipulated positive denominator and positive-definiteness margins make the exact covariance, sandwich, and contrast-variance maps continuous on the inference boxes as well.  The assumed uniform convergence of the tail errors, Taylor-enclosure widths, terminal mesh diameters, and outward-rounding errors therefore implies the following common enclosure property: there is a deterministic sequence \(e_t\downarrow0\) such that every lower endpoint used at stage \(t\) is at least the infimum of its exact scalar target over the relevant leaf minus \(e_t\), and every upper endpoint is at most the corresponding supremum plus \(e_t\).  The analogous operator-norm excess for every required matrix enclosure is at most \(e_t\).  Enlarging \(e_t\) by a fixed finite factor if necessary covers all finitely many kinds of tests.

Let \(\gamma_*>0\) be a common lower bound for the exact wrong-graph objectives on all nonempty wrong-graph comparison products.  Such a number exists by the strict uniform graph-separation hypothesis and finiteness of \(\mathfrak G\).  If
\[
 f_{\boldsymbol d,\boldsymbol d'}(\vartheta,\vartheta')
 =\left\lVert m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
        -m_{\boldsymbol d',\mathcal T}(\vartheta')\right\rVert_W^2,
\]
then \(f_{\boldsymbol d,\boldsymbol d'}\geq\gamma_*\) on every such product.  Consequently, once \(e_t<\gamma_*/2\), every wrong-graph leaf has a strictly positive lower enclosure and passes.  When there is no wrong-graph comparison, both the exact and certified graph bounds are \(+\infty\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}grid\text{-}criterion}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\), so no numerical test is required.

We next prove eventual success of the remote-pair branch without asserting a uniform negative distance margin merely from membership in the open set \(\{D<0\}\).  Fix a graph \(\boldsymbol d\), put
\[
 K_{\boldsymbol d}=\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d},
 \qquad
 D(\vartheta,\vartheta')=lVert\vartheta-\vartheta'\rVert_2^2-r_{\mathrm{id}}^2,
\]
and define
\[
 f(\vartheta,\vartheta')=
 \left\lVert m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
              -m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta')\right\rVert_W^2,
 \qquad
 S=\{x\in K_{\boldsymbol d}:D(x)\geq0\}.
\]
First suppose \(S\neq\varnothing\).  The strict uniform remote slack supplies \(\lambda_*>0\), common over the finitely many nonempty remote tasks, such that
\[
 f(x)\geq\lambda_*\qquad(x\in S).
\]
Let
\[
 U=\{x\in K_{\boldsymbol d}:f(x)>\lambda_*/2\}.
\]
Continuity of \(f\) makes \(U\) relatively open in \(K_{\boldsymbol d}\), and the preceding inequality gives \(S\subset U\).  Hence the complement \(C=K_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U\) is compact and disjoint from \(S\).  Thus \(D<0\) on \(C\).  If \(C\neq\varnothing\), continuity and compactness give the genuine uniform separation
\[
 \delta_{\boldsymbol d}:=-\max_{x\in C}D(x)>0,
 \qquad D(x)\leq-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}\quad(x\in C).
\]
This margin is obtained on the compact complement \(C\), not on the whole open set \(\{D<0\}\).  Uniform continuity of \(D\) on \(K_{\boldsymbol d}\) yields \(a_{\boldsymbol d}>0\) such that
\[
 \lVert x-y\rVert_2<a_{\boldsymbol d}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |D(x)-D(y)|<\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/2.
\]
Consider any closed terminal product leaf \(B\subset K_{\boldsymbol d}\) with diameter below \(a_{\boldsymbol d}\).  If \(B\cap C=\varnothing\), then \(B\subset U\), whence \(f>lambda_*/2\) throughout \(B\); for \(e_t<\lambda_*/4\), its moment-distance lower enclosure is positive and the corrected branch rule passes \(B\), whether or not \(B\) straddles \(D=0\).  If \(B\cap C\neq\varnothing\), choose \(x\in B\cap C\).  For every \(y\in B\),
\[
 D(y)\leq D(x)+|D(y)-D(x)|
 <-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/2.
\]
For \(e_t<\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/4\), the upper enclosure of \(D\) on \(B\) is therefore negative, so the branch discards \(B\).  If \(C=\varnothing\), every leaf is contained in \(U\) and the first case alone applies.  This gives the required finite-cover/mesh argument: once the terminal mesh is smaller than the minimum of the finitely many positive \(a_{\boldsymbol d}\), every leaf lies in the passing case or meets a compact set on which the distance constraint has the displayed negative margin and hence lies in the discard case.  If instead \(S=\varnothing\), compactness directly gives \(\max_{K_{\boldsymbol d}}D=-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}<0\), so all sufficiently accurate leaves are discarded and the remote bound is \(+\infty\).  It follows that every remote tree eventually terminates successfully under precisely the corrected remote-subset rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\).

For the local tests, let \(\mu_*>0\) and \(\kappa_*>0\) be common lower bounds for the stipulated exact chart strong-monotonicity margins and Jacobian singular values.  The deterministic chart trees are assumed eventually to produce a valid cover.  On every resulting chart, the exact symmetric projected-Jacobian matrix has least eigenvalue at least \(\mu_*\), while
\[
 J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}
 J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
 \succeq \kappa_*^2 I.
\]
Uniform derivative-enclosure and rounding convergence makes the corresponding interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests succeed for all sufficiently large \(t\).  Indeed, one may fix positive dyadic numbers strictly below \(\mu_*\) and \(\kappa_*\); the arithmetic-precision mesh eventually contains such test values, and the uniform matrix-enclosure error is eventually smaller than their slack.  The eventual valid-cover hypothesis then supplies the required coverage and co-containment checks.  The same argument, applied to the strict uniform interiority, denominator, pivot, and positive-definiteness margins in the statement, makes every remaining algebraic and covariance test succeed.  The exact rank computation succeeds because \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), and the allocation checks succeed because \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) and every \(\rho_j>0\).

It remains to verify the precision check.  Compactness of the inference boxes and continuity of \(V_\tau\) show that the maximum defining \(v_\tau^\circ\) is finite and attained.  Put
\[
 s_*=N_{\max}-N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ>0.
\]
Uniform convergence of the covariance, derivative, matrix-inverse, and contrast enclosures implies that the recorded variance upper bound \(\max_a(\overline v_\tau)_a\) converges from above to \(v_\tau^\circ\).  Since \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and \(w_{\max}>0\) are fixed, the map
\[
 v\longmapsto z_{1-\alpha/2}^2v/w_{\max}^2
\]
is continuous.  Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(t\),
\[
 N_{\mathrm{req}}(\Xi_t)
 <N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ+s_*/2
 <N_{\max}.
\]

There are finitely many graph tuples and test categories, so the preceding thresholds have a common finite index \(t_0\).  For every \(t\geq t_0\), the syntax and box checks, full-rank and positive-allocation checks, all graph, remote, chart, covariance, interiority, and linear-algebra checks, and the required-well check pass.  The literal return rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak C(\Xi_t)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\qquad(t\geq t_0).
\]
This conclusion is consistent with the unconditional finite termination and one-sided soundness of \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness\text{-}complexity}\).  The proof uses the theorem's stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses only; it does not establish them for either prescribed synthetic benchmark.
